expected.longDescription:
NodeCore is one of the strangest games on Luanti, and that is the reason to play it. Warr1024's game calls itself a surreal dream-world where everything is possible but nothing is easy. It throws out the things block games normally rely on: there is no crafting grid and almost no explanation, so you learn how the world works by pounding on it, moving things around and paying attention to what happens.

All crafting happens in the world itself rather than in a menu. Stack the right things in the right place and strike them, and something new may appear. From those odd beginnings it goes much further than you would expect, with machines built from separate parts, hinged and rotary machinery, automated crafting and even logic circuits that work with light.

Its listing warns of a different kind of difficulty, and that is accurate. There are no monsters to blame, only your own understanding, and progress comes from discovery. It has a built-in new player guide, plays alone or with others, and works with a gamepad or on mobile. The whole thing is a tiny download of about 1.4 MB under the MIT license, and it has been in active development since 2019. Try it if figuring things out is your favourite part of any game.
bestFor: Players who like figuring things out
notFor: Players who want guidance

We'd agree on whether the group wants hints before somebody opens a walkthrough and answers the question everyone else was enjoying.

Choose NodeCore when that process sounds like the evening's entertainment; a player looking for a familiar recipe list and quick equipment progression may find the early uncertainty frustrating.

firstPlaySteps.text: Install Luanti and the NodeCore game, then select NodeCore when creating a new world.
Open the built-in new-player guide and follow its early discoveries before looking for a conventional crafting menu.
Experiment with materials directly in the world. Change one arrangement at a time so you can tell what caused the result.
Keep your first discoveries small and repeatable before attempting a complicated machine.

bestFor: Players who enjoy discovering rules through experiments
Friends who like comparing theories and building together
Builders interested in mechanical and optical systems
notFor: Players expecting familiar Minecraft crafting recipes
Groups that want immediate instructions for every objective

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: Choose a server or shared world running NodeCore, rather than a different Luanti game.
Agree on whether to share solutions or offer hints; discovery is a large part of this game.
Start a shared experimental area before combining unfamiliar mechanisms into a larger build.

expected.longDescription:
Exile is the block game for people who think survival games are too polite. Created by Dokimi and now developed by the Exile Team, it drops you into the wilderness as an outcast with no tools and little hope, and its own listing calls it challenging and at times brutal. There is no gentle first night here: the cold, your hunger and your body will all work against you from the first minute.

Finding food, water and shelter is the whole early game. You craft basic tools, then work up through fires, kilns and furnaces, and the technology stays simple, because progress is measured in staying alive. Hypothermia, exhaustion and disease are all things that can kill you, while seasonal weather, erosion and water that flows through soil make the world feel like a place with no interest in you.

For a harder and slower game, the Carpathian map generator is supported alongside the standard Valleys setting. It is free software on Luanti, with no required add-ons, and it is actively developed. Its developers warn that some people may find parts of it difficult or disturbing, which is fair. Choose it if you want every campfire you survive to feel like an achievement.
bestFor: Players who want a hard, slow survival game
notFor: Players who want a relaxed building game

Use Valleys for a first attempt; the project describes Carpathian as the harder, slower alternative.
Prioritize shelter, a bed and drinking water before committing to a large construction project.
Watch exhaustion and temperature, and use your camp to recover rather than pushing through every warning.

bestFor: Patient survival players
Groups that enjoy dividing practical camp tasks
Players who want shelter and weather to matter
notFor: Relaxed creative-building sessions
Players who dislike demanding survival systems

expected.longDescription:
Asuna is the Luanti game to install if you mostly want somewhere beautiful to wander. EmptyStar has blended many of the platform's best biome and decoration mods into one curated package, and the numbers show how much that adds up to: more than 60 biomes, over 100 flowers, plants and mushrooms, more than 30 farming crops, 27 animals and creatures, and 80 decorative stones to build with.

It leaves the tone up to you, through content packs that can be switched on or off in settings. Nutrition rewards a good diet with faster movement and health regeneration, and starvation is off by default. Wayfarer adds achievements, loot chests and Worldgates, a teleportation network for getting around all that land. Menagerie brings the animals and slimes, Stratosphere adds sky islands and harvestable clouds, and Research offers an earned creative mode, where discovering an item lets you duplicate it.

With 54 achievements and 31 background music tracks, it feels more complete than its peaceful pitch suggests. Mapgen v7 is the only officially supported map generator, and it is the one that produces those sky islands. It is free software, rated very positively by players, and a gentle counterweight to the harsher survival games in this family.
bestFor: Relaxed exploration and building
notFor: Players who want combat-heavy gameplay

Before generating the world, spend a few minutes deciding what kind of trip you want. Asuna's optional content packs make that a meaningful choice. Neither requires turning the whole evening into a fight against hunger.

We'd use mapgen v7 and start with the included content before installing more mods. Asuna already combines and adapts a substantial collection, so adding another copy of a bundled component can create warnings instead of improving the game. Once the group has explored a little, you can decide whether it wants a settled farming-and-building world or a longer expedition. The best reason to choose this edition is having a landscape worth making that decision in.

firstPlaySteps.text: Install Asuna in Luanti and select it as the game for a new world.
Choose mapgen v7, the officially supported generator; the sky-island content depends on it.
Review Settings > Content: Games > Asuna and choose the content packs your group wants before settling into the world.
Try the bundled content first. Avoid adding duplicate versions of mods Asuna already includes.
Explore a few nearby biomes before committing to a building site, and consider Research if gathering repeated building materials becomes a chore.

bestFor: Explorers who enjoy finding a place to build
Groups that want configurable survival rules
Builders interested in earned item duplication
notFor: Players seeking a tightly directed campaign
Groups expecting every third-party Luanti mod to work unchanged

expected.longDescription:
Combined Arms is a very simple idea executed at huge scale: take the best factions in Command & Conquer's history and let them fight in one game. Built on OpenRA, it puts the Allies, Soviets, GDI, Nod and the alien Scrin on the same battlefield, drawing units and technology from Tiberian Dawn, Red Alert and Tiberium Wars. PC Gamer's description of a giant five-faction brawl is about right.

It would be easy for that to fall apart, but this is a designed game rather than a pile of parts. The older Tiberian Dawn sides gain the tech centres, support powers and navies they never had. Each faction also splits into several sub-factions with their own units, super-weapons and support powers, so picking GDI is only the first decision of a match.

You can play skirmishes and multiplayer matches, or try singleplayer and co-operative missions, and the mod has kept growing since its 1.0 release in December 2023, with a major overhaul in August 2024 and further updates since. Best of all for newcomers, it is free and completely standalone: you need neither an original Command & Conquer game nor anything else installed. It runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.
bestFor: Experienced RTS players
notFor: Beginners to the genre

Start a skirmish and pick a familiar faction while learning this edition's units and options.
Read the faction section of the release notes when returning after an update.

bestFor: Friends with different favourite C&C factions
Skirmish players who enjoy experimenting with army composition
Returning RTS players willing to relearn familiar units

expected.longDescription:
Crystallized Nexus is a reimagining of the old Crystallized Doom mod, and it is one of the more technically ambitious things anyone has done with OpenRA. DoGyAUT's standalone real-time strategy game pits GDI against Nod in a Tiberian Sun-style war, and much of its appeal is a battlefield that actively changes under you.

Terrain matters here. Weapon and sight ranges scale with height, units slow down going uphill and speed up on the way down, cliffs can be collapsed to open new paths, and weapons can deform the ground itself. Ion storms roll through in phases, granting effects and throwing random lightning at everyone. Blue and red Tiberium chain-react when hit, and veinholes can be destroyed, leaving a pit you can walk through.

The rest of the design is just as busy, with mob squads that share a health pool, formation movement, and units that dodge when a crusher approaches. Bots come in profiles from Rush to Adaptive, across difficulty tiers from Easy to Brutal, and an adaptive soundtrack shifts with the fighting. It is a playtest build rather than a finished release, so expect changes and rough edges. It is free, self-contained and open source under the GPL version 3, with no other game needed.
bestFor: Players who like trying new RTS games
notFor: Players who want a finished game - it is a playtest

expected.longDescription:
Westwood's Red Alert 2 is one of the best-loved games in the Command & Conquer series, and this edition brings it to OpenRA through Romanov's Vengeance, the project by MustaphaTR that took over where OpenRA's own unfinished Red Alert 2 work left off. Allied and Soviet armies are here with their famous excess intact, and it goes further than the base game by adding Yuri's Revenge content as well.

Running on OpenRA changes the experience around those battles. You get high frame rates on modern displays, current netcode and an updated lobby, which is exactly what makes a 2000 game worth setting up for an evening with friends. The mod's developers have also taken liberties that the original never did, such as adding new subfactions, so this is its own take on Red Alert 2 rather than a strict recreation.

That makes it a good fit for people who want Prism Tanks, Apocalypse Tanks and a working multiplayer lobby without fighting an old executable. If you want the game exactly as it shipped, the differences may bother you. It is open source under the GPL version 3, and development happens in the open on GitHub, which is the best place to follow its progress.
bestFor: Red Alert 2 fans
notFor: Players who want a finished feature set

expected.longDescription:
Tiberian Dawn HD is an experiment in having the best of both worlds: EA's remastered 2020 art, on OpenRA's engine and netcode. It is an official OpenRA project that runs Command & Conquer's first war using the high-definition sprites from the Remastered Collection, while keeping OpenRA's modern controls, lobby and balance. Multiplayer is still compatible with OpenRA.

The important catch is what it needs from you. The mod loads its art directly from an existing digital install of the C&C Remastered Collection, so you must own that game on Steam or Origin. Without it, there is nothing here to look at. A dedicated graphics card is recommended too, because all those high-resolution assets are heavy.

The project's own readme is candid about its status. It calls itself a prototype and a proof of concept, says performance, memory use and loading times have not been optimised, and warns you to proceed at your own risk. So treat this as a good-looking curiosity for owners of the Remastered Collection, rather than the stable way to play. For that, the official OpenRA edition is the better choice. It is open source under the GPL version 3, but no formal releases have been published.
bestFor: Fans of the original C&C
notFor: Players who want new factions

Confirm the required data is present before launching the prototype.
Use a dedicated GPU as recommended by the project, and expect unoptimized loading and memory use.

bestFor: Remastered Collection owners curious about OpenRA
Players who enjoy testing experimental presentation

expected.longDescription:
HoloCure is a fan game with far more care in it than anybody could reasonably expect. Kay Yu's completely free and unofficial game takes the Vampire Survivors formula and fills it with Hololive VTubers, and its enormous rating, 4.9 out of 5 from over 5,000 people on itch.io, suggests that you do not need to know who any of them are to get hooked. There is no monetisation of any kind.

You pick a character, walk around and try to survive endless waves of enemies while your attacks fire on their own. The decisions come from building your run: which weapons and passive items you take as you level up, and how they combine. A session lasts about half an hour, so it is easy to tell yourself just one more. There are 47 characters to unlock through a gacha system that uses only in-game currency, each with unique skills and special attacks, along with song remixes by Eufrik that are good enough to listen to on their own.

It is not affiliated with Hololive or Cover Corp, and it is still in development, with no mobile version planned. This official edition is the plain single-player game on Windows. For playing together, PlayBound's co-op edition is listed separately. It supports English, Japanese and Indonesian.
bestFor: Short action sessions
Hololive fans
notFor: Players wanting multiplayer - see the PlayBound edition

expected.longDescription:
HoloCure is a great single-player game, and this edition makes it possible to share with friends. It adds PippleCultist's HoloCure Multiplayer Mod to Save the Fans!, so a group can run stages together, with PlayBound installing the Aurie mod loader and the mod in a single click. Surviving those waves of enemies is an entirely different kind of chaos when somebody else is filling the screen with attacks too.

The mod itself works over LAN, with one player hosting and everyone else joining on the same network. PlayBound's party system removes that limit: Join Game puts every member on one shared Connect network and points HoloCure at it, so a LAN session works across the internet. In the game, you go to Play, then Multiplayer, then the saved network adapter, then Host LAN Session for the leader and Join LAN Session for everyone else.

Some of the mod's menus only work with a mouse, which is worth knowing if you are on a controller. This is also experimental community software rather than an official HoloCure feature, and the mod's author notes that it may crash occasionally because so much of the game is modified to add networking. Your saves stay in their usual folder, and you can go back to the unmodded game at any time. If you only want to play alone, use the official edition.
bestFor: Co-op groups
notFor: Players who need a stable, polished multiplayer

credits.role: Author of the HoloCure Multiplayer Mod

credits.role: Mod loader the multiplayer mod runs on

Keep the distinction between installation convenience and mod compatibility clear. Back up your save before changing versions, use matching game and mod builds, and avoid adding unrelated mods until the shared session works. We'd choose this with friends who can laugh off a failed attempt and are interested enough in HoloCure to try again.

Install this multiplayer edition and launch it through PlayBound.

expected.longDescription:
Daggerfall Unity is the reason most people can comfortably play The Elder Scrolls II today. It rebuilds Bethesda's 1996 role-playing game in the Unity engine while using the original game's own data, so the enormous world, its towns and dungeons and its quests all remain Daggerfall, without the need to run it through a DOS emulator.

The practical differences start with the platform: it runs natively on Windows, Linux and macOS, with mouselook and modern input in place of the old DOS setup. The original's assets are still required, but they are free, and PlayBound sets them up for you during install.

Its real strength is the mod scene the rebuild made possible. DREAM reworks the textures, sounds and interface; Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul changes how fights resolve; World of Daggerfall fills out the sparse countryside; and quest packs add new things to do. The base game asks for little, just a Skylake-era i3 and 2 GB of RAM, though a long mod list can raise that a lot. The project is open source under the MIT license, with its development discussed on the Workshop forums and on Discord.
bestFor: RPG fans curious about the series' roots
Players who want Daggerfall with modern controls and mods
notFor: Players who want quick, linear games
Players who want the original DOS engine - choose Classic DOS

The first decision is how much you want to change. We'd run a clean installation before choosing a graphics overhaul or a long mod list. That gives you a working baseline and a chance to learn which parts of Daggerfall you actually want to adjust. The engine can keep the old presentation through its retro display modes, so modern controls do not force you into a wholesale visual replacement.

When you do add mods, add them gradually and pay attention to their own instructions. The developer's hardware figures describe the engine, not every combination of community textures, world additions and gameplay changes. If performance drops or a problem appears after a new addition, knowing what changed is much more useful than starting again with an equally large collection. For us, that flexibility is the attraction: you can preserve the adventure's older character while choosing how much friction to remove.

If prompted for data, select the original game-data folder rather than the Unity executable folder.
Launch without optional mods first and check movement, camera and display settings.
Choose a modern or retro presentation before building a mod list.
Add optional mods gradually, following their requirements and keeping saves backed up.

Players who want to choose their own mod setup
Windows, macOS and Linux users seeking a native engine
notFor: Players expecting modern Elder Scrolls quest design

Sometimes you want another crack at a dungeon that has been kicking your teeth in, with a little more power on your side. Rat King Pixel Dungeon 2 is built around that feeling. Zrp200's Shattered Pixel Dungeon fork buffs the heroes and puts the Rat King himself in the character lineup. A joke that began around April Fools has become a whole alternative way to play.

The appeal is getting more room to experiment. If you keep finding interesting equipment in Shattered and dying before you get much use out of it, this is the edition we'd point you toward. Stronger characters give you a different starting point for exploring the dungeon's possibilities. Challenges are still there when you want to turn the pressure back up.

Choose this one for the powerful-hero approach. Rat King Adventure, its descendant, piles on more systems and a whole extra endgame. Our preference would be to get comfortable here before adding that much to learn. PlayBound installs the project's Java desktop release and prepares a runtime if needed. Android players can grab the separate build from the developer.
bestFor: Players who like build experiments
notFor: Players who want classic difficulty

expected.longDescription:
Beat Yog and still want to see what your character can do? Rat King Adventure has an answer. Its Abyss carries on beyond that boss, with tougher enemies and no fixed end. That is a pretty good introduction to this fork's priorities. There is always another reason to push a run further.

Adventure builds on Rat King Pixel Dungeon 2, then adds tier-six weapons, expanded talents and secret subclasses for each class. The special seeds are particularly interesting. They can change the rules of a run, giving you a reason to revisit familiar ground with a different plan. Kromers bring another temptation, offering unpredictable rewards with a risk attached. For the player who reads an item description and immediately starts thinking of combinations, there is plenty to get stuck into.

We'd recommend learning Shattered or RKPD2 first. This edition adds enough moving parts that knowing the basics will make the discoveries more satisfying. Come here when you want more to figure out and somewhere to take a strong character after the usual finish. PlayBound uses the project's Java desktop release. The developer also distributes an Android build.
bestFor: Veterans
notFor: Newcomers

There is a particular pleasure in returning to an old Tomb Raider room and remembering where you need to go before you remember how to get there. OpenLara is for that sort of return visit. XProger's open-source engine takes the classic games as its starting point, with the first Tomb Raider the sensible place to begin.

The distinction between the available engine builds matters. In the project's roadmap, XProger describes the original main-branch engine as capable of completing Tomb Raider I, while the newer engine rewrite has its own unfinished milestones. Support for later games is part of that ongoing work. We'd start with the first adventure and treat experiments with the sequels as something to investigate separately.

This edition installs the standalone Windows release from the project's GitHub downloads. The website you linked is also the home of its WebGL demo, which is a handy way to get a first look. Linux and macOS builds are published separately. Our pick here is for people who enjoy revisiting a classic through a community engine and are comfortable checking the project notes when they hit a rough edge. For release downloads and troubleshooting, follow the XProger links on this page.
bestFor: Tomb Raider fans
notFor: Players wanting the original look only
